key_insight: Synchronized iterative retrieval-and-reasoning loops can outperform an idealized static 'Gold Context' RAG in scientific multi-hop question answering under realistic conditions (sparse domain knowledge and heterogeneous evidence). This shows iteration can assemble complementary evidence that a single static context cannot.
problem_solved: Determines when and why iterative RAG actually surpasses a static upper-bound RAG for scientific multi-hop QA, isolating the mechanisms and conditions that enable gains.
method: Controlled, mechanism-level diagnostic comparisons between iterative retrieval–reasoning loops and an idealized static (Gold Context) RAG setup.
Systematic ablations varying evidence properties (sparsity, heterogeneity) and synchronization of retrieval+reasoning to identify which factors drive iterative gains.
Quantitative experiments showing stepwise evidence assembly by iteration yields higher accuracy in the settings identified as favorable.
impact: Provides practical guidance for when to invest in iterative retrieval pipelines versus building larger static contexts, improving design choices for domain-specific multi-hop QA systems and reducing wasted engineering effort.
visual_elements: Side-by-side flow diagram: iterative retrieval→reasoning loop vs static Gold Context pipeline to show procedural differences.
Bar/line chart: accuracy comparison across conditions (homogeneous vs heterogeneous evidence; dense vs sparse knowledge).
Evidence-assembly Sankey or stepwise diagram: how multiple retrieval steps combine complementary snippets to answer a multi-hop question.
Decision flowchart: recommended conditions for choosing iterative RAG vs static RAG (based on evidence heterogeneity and knowledge sparsity).
paper_title: When Iterative RAG Beats Ideal Evidence: A Diagnostic Study in Scientific Multi-hop Question Answering
paper_authors: Mahdi Astaraki, Mohammad Arshi Saloot, Ali Shiraee Kasmaee, Hamidreza Mahyar, Soheila Samiee
